F01.P1.justification: const int n = 7; return n; — const local binding, no annotation needed.

F01.P2.fragment:
long long counter = 0;
constexpr long long LIMIT = 100;
F01.P2.justification: namespace-scope `int64_t counter = 0;` (mutable, reassignable) and `constexpr int64_t LIMIT = 100;` (compile-time constant).

F02.P1.justification: `int32_t v; if(cond){v=5;}else{v=9;} return v;` — C++ permits declaration without initializer; definite assignment on both branches makes subsequent read well-defined.

F02.P2.justification: `unsigned char buf[16]; buf[0]=1; return buf[0];` — local array of trivial type is default-initialized (indeterminate value) without an initializer per [dcl.init].

F03.P1.justification: `x += 1;` in-place compound assignment, fewest-token form per R10.

F04.P1.justification: `int slot=4; int& port = slot; port=9; return slot;` — lvalue reference is a writable alias.

F04.P2.justification: `std::span<const int> window(xs); return window[0];` — C++20 std::span is a non-owning, non-copying read-only view.

F04.P3.justification: Heap-allocated object via `new`, second handle obtained by routing through a one-element `std::vector<Obj*>`, identity compared with pointer equality `first==second` (reference/pointer identity, not value equality).

F05.P1.justification: `f(x)` bare call, `x` a std::vector<int> passed with no sigil — plainest ordinary call-site form.

F05.P2.justification: `void put(int& c){c=12;} ... put(cell); return cell;` — reference parameter is C++'s dedicated writable-alias-passing form.

F05.P3.justification: Lambda `auto neg = [k](int a){return k-a;};` captures enclosing local `k`, passed by name to `std::transform` (standard higher-order sequence operation).

F06.P1.justification: `int mid(const std::vector<int>& xs){return xs[1];} auto y = mid(xs); return y;`

F06.P2.justification: `std::pair<int,int> divmod2(int a,int b){return {a/b,a%b};} auto [q,r]=divmod2(a,b); return q+r;` — structured bindings destructure the pair at the call site.

F07.P1.justification: `auto r = a*b+c;` ordinary precedence, no redundant parens.

F07.P2.justification: `auto q=a/b; auto m=a%b; double d = (double)a/b;` — truncating integer division, C++ % takes sign of dividend, explicit cast for real division.

F08.P1.justification: No std checked/wrapping/saturating integer op exists in C++20 (rungs i-iii unavailable); rung iv (plain `m+1` operator) used per canonical_task's own explicit preference order, which permits this fallback. C++ has no checked arithmetic mode (toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause records this as a language fact, not a recipe deviation); overflow is UB, scored by metrics B/D not by support level.

F08.P2.justification: Rung ii used: `int q; if(b==0){q=0;}else{q=a/b;}` — no std checked-division operation exists in C++20 std lib (rung i unavailable).

F09.P2.fragment:
std::sort(xs.begin(), xs.end(), std::greater<int>());
bool lt = (a < b);
F09.P2.justification: `std::sort(xs.begin(),xs.end(),std::greater<int>());` explicit descending comparator (in-place, mutates xs); `bool lt = a<b;`

F10.P1.justification: `int32_t small = static_cast<int32_t>(big);` explicit narrowing conversion (rung ii); C++20 `std::in_range<int32_t>(big)` also available for a checked-style guard.

F10.P2.justification: `double sum = i + d;` — implicit usual-arithmetic-conversion promotes `i` to double, no explicit cast required or written.

F11.P1.justification: `int e = xs[i]; return e;` — std::vector::operator[] ordinary indexed read (UB on out-of-range, unchecked).

F11.P2.justification: `std::vector<int> part(xs.begin()+1, xs.begin()+4); return part[0];` — range-constructor sub-range (copies elements).

F12.P1.justification: `std::optional<int> o = std::nullopt; int n = o.value_or(0); return n;` — std::optional (C++17) is a documented type-level absent-value construct with standard fallback form.

F12.P2.justification: C++20 std::optional has no monadic and_then/transform (added only in C++23; frozen recipe is c++20). No standard optional-aware chaining/mapping operation is available, so per R9/na named-substitution rule the explicit conditional is written instead: `int p_val; if(o.has_value()) p_val=h(o.value()); else { /*absent*/ } int result = o.has_value()? h(o.value()) : 0;`. Scored PARTIAL under P-a (substituted weaker mechanism), never FULL, per canonical_task's own named substitution clause.

F13.P1.justification: `int parse_twice(const std::string& s){ return std::stoi(s)*2; }` — std::stoi throws std::invalid_argument/std::out_of_range on failure; unhandled, it propagates automatically to the caller.

F13.P2.justification: `int n; try { n = std::stoi(s); } catch(...) { n = 0; } return n;` — try/catch is C++'s local-handling construct.

F14.P1.justification: `using Shape = std::variant<Circle,Rect>; Shape s = Circle{2.0};` — std::variant (C++17) is a closed alternative set fixed at the type's declaration; no code elsewhere can add a third alternative to this Shape alias.

F14.P2.justification: `double area = std::visit(AreaVisitor{}, s);` with a visitor struct providing `operator()` overloads for both Circle and Rect, no default arm; std::visit requires the visitor be callable for every alternative in the variant, so an unhandled alternative is a compile error (exhaustiveness enforced statically).

F14.P3.justification: Abstract base `struct ShapeBase { virtual double area() const = 0; };` with Circle/Rect implementations in unit `shapes`; a new `Tri : ShapeBase` implementing area() is added in a separate translation unit without editing `shapes`, called through `ShapeBase&`/pointer. Uses the frozen multi-unit recipe (toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes).

F15.P1.justification: `template<typename T> T head(const std::vector<T>& xs){ return xs[0]; }` — template result type is exactly T, not erased/boxed; used at int and std::string.

F15.P2.justification: `template<std::totally_ordered T> T max_of(T a, T b){ return a>b?a:b; }` — C++20 concept `std::totally_ordered` is a declaration-site constraint.

F15.P3.justification: Abstract `struct Named { virtual std::string tag() const = 0; };`, concrete A/B, `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Named>> items` holding one of each, `items[0]->tag()` dispatched at runtime via vtable, concrete type not recoverable from the declared element type Named.

F16.P1.justification: `std::vector<int> xs{1,2,3}; int total = std::accumulate(xs.begin(),xs.end(),0); return total;` — std::accumulate is the standard fold/sum operation (documented in <numeric>).

F16.P2.justification: `std::map<std::string,int> mp{{"a",1}}; int total=0; for(auto&[k,v]:mp) total+=v; auto it=mp.find("b"); int miss = it!=mp.end()? it->second : 0; return total+miss;` — std::map has a documented sorted iteration order (unlike std::unordered_map).

F17.P1.justification: `int read_all(){ std::ifstream f("data.txt"); std::string text((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(f)),std::istreambuf_iterator<char>()); return (int)text.size(); }` — std::ifstream's destructor (RAII) closes the handle on every scope exit, including exceptions.

F17.P2.justification: `struct Handle{ int id; ~Handle(){ ++released; } }; { Handle h{1}; } return released;` — C++ destructors run deterministically and exactly once at end of object lifetime.

F18.P1.justification: `#include <iostream>` then `std::cout << "x\n";` — include makes std::cout available; iostream's the standard console facility.

F18.P2.justification: Unit `util.cpp`: `int secret(){return 1;}` given internal linkage via an anonymous namespace or `static`, plus exported `int pub_add(int a,int b){return a+b+secret();}` declared in util.hpp; external call `util::pub_add(2,3)` (or free-function form) from a separate translation unit using the frozen multi-unit recipe. Internal linkage prevents `secret` from being referenced outside its translation unit ([basic.link]).

F19.P1.justification: `auto fut1=std::async(std::launch::async,[]{return 20;}); auto fut2=std::async(std::launch::async,[]{return 22;}); int sum=fut1.get()+fut2.get();` — std::async/std::future (<future>) is the standard concurrency facility.

F19.P2.justification: `std::atomic<int64_t> counter{0};` incremented via `counter.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed)` from two `std::thread`s, 1000 times each, then joined; std::atomic's read-modify-write operations are documented atomic and race-free ([atomics.types.generic]).

F20.P1.justification: `#include <cstdlib> ... int r = abs(-3); return r;` — <cstdlib>'s `abs` is a C-linkage (extern "C") declaration; C++ calls C functions natively without a separate binding-generator step, satisfying the built-in FFI mechanism requirement.

F20.P2.fragment: extern "C" int add2(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
F20.P2.justification: `extern "C" int add2(int a,int b){ return a+b; }` — extern "C" gives C calling convention and an unmangled external symbol `add2` (verifiable with `nm`).
